primitives.name: Rebound Mechanism
primitives.verbatim_quote: If the quarterback receives the ball before it reaches the top of its arc, the upward motion of the ball strikes the hands, producing what is known as fighting the ball—that is, the ball rebounds from the hands.

primitives.assumptions: Contact between ball and hands is elastic; rebound direction depends on angle of incidence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when $ v_{\text{hand}} > v_{\text{ball}} $ or premature contact before apex.

The core dynamics of football pass reception involve a geometric and kinematic framework defined by the ball’s parabolic arc and the quarterback’s hand positioning. The arc apex represents the critical moment where vertical velocity vanishes, enabling precise hand alignment. Receiving the ball before the apex introduces upward momentum that can cause rebound, a failure mode linked to fumbles. Delayed hand positioning below the apex increases time loss, reducing tactical response window. These principles form a dual system: one of spatial alignment (hand placement), and another of temporal coordination (timing). Each primitive encodes a distinct failure mode—misalignment, premature contact, and delayed action—each contributing to a stochastic model of pass success or failure. The interplay of these variables creates a structured phase space for predictive modeling.
